canonicalExplanation.summary: User input is untrusted: it can be empty, too long, not a number, or out of range. The robust pattern is: **read a whole line** with `fgets(buf, sizeof buf, stdin)`, which never writes past the buffer; **check its return** (NULL means end of input or an error); **handle the newline** (and lines too long to fit); then **convert** with `strtol`, checking that **digits were consumed**, **nothing but whitespace follows**, and the value is **in range** (and `errno` isn't `ERANGE`). Avoid `scanf("%s")` (no size limit) and ignoring `scanf`'s return value: on bad input the variable is left unchanged and the bad characters stay in the stream.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner asks for an age with `scanf("%d", &age)`. A user types "twelve". scanf returns 0, age keeps its garbage value, the letters stay in the input, and the next prompt fails instantly, forever. A line is read with fgets into a bounded array, its newline is handled, and strtol validates complete numeric conversion and range. In this lesson you'll implement a console input loop that rejects malformed and out-of-range values safely.

```predict
{"question": "`scanf(\"%d\", &age)` gets \"abc\". What does it return, and what is age?", "options": ["1, and age is 0", "0, and age is unchanged (possibly uninitialised garbage)"], "answer": 1, "why": "Always check how many items scanf converted."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Operators and precedence**, **Iteration**, **while, do and for** and **Conversions and numeric boundaries**.

sections.heading: The rule: bounded line, full conversion, range check
What counts as valid?

includes: Read lines with fgets into bounded buffers and check every return value.
Convert with strtol, verifying complete conversion, errno and range, and reprompt on bad input.

outcomes: Implement a console input loop that rejects malformed and out-of-range values safely.

examples.title: Reading an age safely
examples.situation: A line is read with fgets into a bounded array, its newline is handled, and strtol validates complete numeric conversion and range.
walkthrough: **A line is read with fgets into a bounded array:** line[64] can never overflow.
**Its newline is handled:** a missing newline means the input was too long, so the rest is discarded.
**strtol validates complete numeric conversion and range:** "twelve" and "42abc" are rejected, 200 fails the 0 to 130 range, and "12" will be accepted.
examples.result: Bad input produces a helpful message and a new prompt, never a stuck loop.

examples.title: The endless prompt
examples.situation: A loop `while (scanf("%d", &n) != 1) puts("Try again");` prints "Try again" forever after one bad input.
walkthrough: scanf leaves the bad characters in the input buffer.
Each retry sees the same "abc" and fails again.
Switch to fgets + strtol, which consumes the whole line each time.
examples.result: One bad line produces one message, and the user can try again.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: scanf with %s or %d always writes a usable value, so its return result and destination width can be ignored.
misconceptions.correction: scanf returns how many items it converted. On failure it leaves the variable unchanged and the bad input in the stream, and %s without a width can overflow the buffer.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In the opening predict, what was age after "abc"?

analogy.example: Reading input safely is like **a bouncer at a door**. They let in one person at a time through a narrow door (bounded fgets), check the ID is real and complete (strtol end check), check the age is allowed (range), and politely turn away everyone else, without letting the queue get stuck.
limitations: Bouncers can ask questions; programs can only reprompt.
A fake ID that's partly real ("42abc") still fails.

steps.explanation: strtol validates complete numeric conversion and rejects text.
The range check rejects values the program can't accept.
A line read with fgets into a bounded array, with its newline handled, is accepted.

trace.textAlternative: Tracing validated input. Step 1, Reject text: end is == line; message is Not a whole number.. strtol validates complete numeric conversion and rejects text. Step 2, Reject range: v is 200; range is 0..130. The range check rejects values the program can't accept. Step 3, Accept: age is 12; return is true. A line read with fgets into a bounded array, with its newline handled, is accepted.

nearTransfer.prompt: Use read_int to ask for a month (1 to 12). Test with 7, 0, 13, "seven", "7x", an empty line, a 100-character line and end of input (Ctrl+D or Ctrl+Z).
scaffold: End of input should stop cleanly.

farTransfer.prompt: Build a small menu program that repeatedly reads a choice and two numbers, using only fgets and strtol/strtod, with full validation and a clean exit on end of input. Compile with -Wall -Wextra and test malicious inputs.

remediation.explanation: For every input call ask: **is the destination bounded, is the return value checked, was the whole input converted, and is the value in range?**

recap.summary: To implement a safe input loop, read whole lines with fgets into bounded buffers, check for end of input and over-long lines, convert with strtol while checking that digits were consumed, only whitespace remains, errno isn't ERANGE and the value is in range, and reprompt on anything else.
